description: Capture the investigation, the confirmed root-cause candidate, the applied defensive fix, the leads that were RULED OUT with evidence, and the diagnostic steps for the reporter, in a findings document the orchestrator can paste into the PR description for issue #6827. The live symptom (Windows desktop, 50+ skills, local git-clone knowledge sources, Telegram, RSS 600MB->3GB in ~10 min, no user interaction) cannot be reproduced in this Linux sandbox with no external network, so the PR must clearly separate what was PROVEN from source, what was FIXED, and what still needs a real-environment repro to confirm. This document also records the exact diagnostic the issue comment asks the reporter to run (set memory.embedding_provider to "", restart, watch for 10 min; capture tracemalloc or py-spy a few minutes into the climb; note smooth vs stepped growth) and points at the existing kiro_crew/perf_sampler.py py-spy support. Depends on FEAT-002 (documents its fix); independent of nothing else.
steps: Create docs/investigations/6827-gateway-memory.md (create the directory if absent). Structure: Summary; What was reproduced (nothing live - state the sandbox constraints explicitly); Root-cause candidate; Fix applied; Leads ruled out with evidence; Diagnostics for the reporter; What still needs real-environment confirmation.

Root-cause candidate section: document the ~1.24 GB eager self.scores buffer in the vendored Llama for the embedding model (n_batch=n_ctx=2048 * n_vocab ~151k * 4 bytes), that the embedding path never reads self.scores, and how this aligns with related issue #6216 (growth appears once the in-process embedding path is active; stable baseline ~606 MB). Cite exact files/line areas: src/kiro_crew/embeddings.py _load_model, src/kiro_crew/_vendor/llama_cpp/llama.py scores allocation (~lines 476-478) and embed() (~lines 1060-1185).
Fix applied section: summarize the FEAT-002 change (reduced n_batch for the embedder, buffer-size math, unchanged n_ctx/n_ubatch and therefore unchanged vectors) and its unit test.

Leads ruled out (with evidence): (a) per-embed KV-cache growth - Llama.embed() calls kv_cache_clear()+reset() every call (llama.py ~lines 1103-1180); (b) compute-thread-pool-per-caller-thread leak - already mitigated by the single owned kc-embed-infer thread (embeddings.py LlamaCppEmbedder docstring/_infer_loop); (c) embed result cache unbounded - bounded by functools.lru_cache(maxsize=_EMBED_CACHE_MAX=128) (embeddings.py ~line 2151); (d) skills held per-session as parsed objects - SkillsLoader caches (_fm_cache/_iter_cache) are shared and keyed by file path with TTL/invalidation, not per-session (skills.py ~lines 1493-1774); (e) folder_watcher retaining per-file buffers for local git clones - state is in SQLite folder_file_state with batched last_seen flushes, no unbounded in-memory accumulation (knowledge/folder_watcher.py scan loop ~lines 380-540); (f) MCP/LLM subprocess fan-out (knowledge/llm_pool.py spawns kiro-cli workers) is issue #3259, explicitly out of scope. For each, name the file and the concrete reason it is bounded.

Diagnostics-for-reporter section: the exact steps from the issue comment - set memory.embedding_provider to "" in config.json, restart, watch python.exe for 10 min (stays ~600MB => consolidate with #6216; still climbs => distinct leak, keep open). Note that this repo already ships py-spy support in src/kiro_crew/perf_sampler.py for capturing a dump a few minutes into the climb, and ask whether growth is smooth or stepped.

What still needs confirmation: state that the fix reduces a large baseline allocation but that whether it fully resolves the 3GB climb requires a real Windows desktop repro with 50+ skills, local git-clone knowledge sources, and Telegram enabled - which the sandbox cannot run. List follow-up measurements the maintainer/reporter should take post-fix.
acceptance_criteria: docs/investigations/6827-gateway-memory.md exists and contains all seven sections with concrete file/line citations for every claim.
The doc explicitly states the live symptom was not reproduced and why (Linux sandbox, INTEGRATIONS_ONLY, no model download), so the PR description does not overclaim.
The doc records the memory.embedding_provider="" diagnostic and the py-spy/tracemalloc capture request verbatim in intent, and points at src/kiro_crew/perf_sampler.py.
Every 'ruled out' lead names the specific file and the reason it is bounded.
verification: Read back docs/investigations/6827-gateway-memory.md and confirm each of the seven sections is present and that ruled-out leads cite real files that exist in the tree.
Confirm no source code is changed by this feature (docs only).
findings:

--- Accuracy checks against source before writing ---
- Confirmed scores allocation shape (n_ctx if logits_all==True else n_batch, n_vocab) at src/kiro_crew/_vendor/llama_cpp/llama.py lines ~476-478 (read directly).
- Confirmed the FEAT-002 fix as committed: _N_BATCH = 1_536 constant + block comment at embeddings.py ~lines 109-138; embedder is the sole in-repo Llama constructor (vendored file untouched).
- Confirmed _EMBED_CACHE_MAX = 128 at embeddings.py line 2154, applied via functools.lru_cache(maxsize=_EMBED_CACHE_MAX) on _cached_embed (~line 2181); _MAX_EMBED_CHARS = 6_000 at line 138.
- Verified every ruled-out lead cites a real file that exists in the tree: perf_sampler.py, skills.py, knowledge/folder_watcher.py, knowledge/llm_pool.py, embeddings.py, _vendor/llama_cpp/llama.py all present (ls confirmed).

--- Content notes ---
- Buffer math stated verbatim from FEAT-002 findings: old 2048*151936*4 = 1.24 GB, new 1536*151936*4 = 0.93 GB, reclaim ~311 MB.
- Sandbox non-repro constraints stated plainly (Linux, INTEGRATIONS_ONLY, no PyPI, no 610MB model), and the doc separates PROVEN / FIXED / NEEDS-REPRO so the PR does not overclaim.
- Reporter diagnostic recorded: set memory.embedding_provider to "", restart, 10-min watch (stays ~600MB => consolidate with #6216; still climbs => distinct leak, keep #6827 open); asks for tracemalloc/py-spy a few minutes into the climb via src/kiro_crew/perf_sampler.py and whether growth is smooth or stepped.
- Related issue #6216 and out-of-scope subprocess issue #3259 both referenced as specified.
